key_insight: Human and LLM-generated synthesis recipes performed comparably in closed-loop experiments, and their collaboration helped discover a new material prototype (Ba3PtO5) in the Ruddlesden-Popper/RSP phase space.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests LLMs can accelerate materials synthesis planning when paired with experimental validation, especially for exploring structured but underexploited compositional spaces.
method: Generated synthesis recipes with humans and LLMs for known and unknown Ruddlesden-Popper candidates
Tested recipe success through in-lab experimentation
Fed results back into a closed-loop human/LLM collaboration across two rounds
evidence_signal: Recipe success rates were similar between humans and LLMs, with high performance on known materials and much lower but nonzero success on unknown materials across both rounds.
watch_item: Performance drops sharply on unknown targets, so LLM-generated plans still require careful experimental screening and domain expertise before scale-up.
paper_title: Human and LLM Collaboration for Accelerated Materials Synthesis and Discovery
